title: Paid to Let Go
endLine: Protons turn the rotor; the turning pays mainly to release ATP.

scenes.tts: We have watched poisons block the proton flow, or let it leak around A T P synthase. Now look inside. Protons fall through, and A T P comes out. How does a falling proton pay for a chemical bond?
scenes.narration: We have watched poisons block the proton flow, or let it leak around ATP synthase. Now look inside. Protons fall through, and ATP comes out. How does a falling proton pay for a chemical bond?
scenes.caption: We have watched poisons block the proton flow, or let it leak around ATP synthase. Now look inside. Protons fall through, and ATP comes out. How does a falling proton pay for a chemical bond?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's 16:9 world and colour map without a reset. COLOUR BY CONCEPT, as before: protons YELLOW dots; electron transport chain BLUE; ATP synthase and ATP GREEN (ATP as small GREEN squares); ADP GOLD dots; membrane and axes GREY; neutral labels TEXT white. New in this film: phosphate as small ORANGE dots, and the rotating parts of the synthase (c-ring and gamma shaft) in bright GREEN while the fixed parts (a subunit, head) are pale green-grey with GREEN outlines. As in the first film, the horizontal GREY membrane band crosses the frame, the crowded side with many YELLOW protons is ABOVE (intermembrane space) and the matrix is BELOW. A small 'schematic' tag sits at bottom right all film. No molecular structures: labelled blocks, rings and dots only. Opening frame: the first film's layout, BLUE chain block at left in the membrane, GREEN synthase at right (small block in the membrane, rounded head below it in the matrix), YELLOW protons crowded above. On 'block the proton flow', a brief RED plug flashes in the synthase's membrane block and fades; on 'leak around', a brief RED leak channel flashes beside it and fades (both are ghosts of the first film, gone for good after this sentence). On 'look inside', the camera pushes in on the synthase until it fills about 70% of the frame height; the BLUE chain slides out of frame. On 'Protons fall through', YELLOW dots drop into the membrane block one at a time; on 'ATP comes out', GOLD dots enter the head and GREEN squares leave it. On the question, large white text across the top: 'How does a proton pay?'
Title 'Paid to Let Go' fades in above the enlarged synthase for 2 s while the question text fades out. YELLOW protons keep dropping in slowly; GREEN squares keep leaving the head.

scenes.tts: In the membrane, a ring of c subunits, the rotor, presses against a fixed a subunit. A proton enters a half channel and lands on an acid on the ring. Only a loaded subunit can turn into the oily membrane.
scenes.narration: In the membrane, a ring of c subunits, the rotor, presses against a fixed a subunit. A proton enters a half channel and lands on an acid on the ring. Only a loaded subunit can turn into the oily membrane.
scenes.caption: In the membrane, a ring of c subunits, the rotor, presses against a fixed a subunit. A proton enters a half channel and lands on an acid on the ring. Only a loaded subunit can turn into the oily membrane.
scenes.visual: The synthase's membrane block transforms into its parts, side view: a bright GREEN ring drawn as a short drum of 8 vertical segments, labelled 'c-ring rotor', and a pale fixed block pressed against its right side labelled 'a subunit (fixed)'. On 'half channel', a narrow tunnel lights inside the a subunit, open to the upper side only; one YELLOW proton slides down it and sits on a small notch on the facing ring segment (the acid, drawn as a notch, no structure). On 'only a loaded subunit', that loaded segment turns away from the a subunit into the grey membrane; an empty segment beside it stays put, a small RED cross flashing on the membrane where it would have to go.

scenes.tts: The gradient biases the ring's random jostling, so it steps mostly one way. Nearly a full turn later, the proton leaves into the matrix. The ring is bolted to a bent shaft, gamma.
scenes.narration: The gradient biases the ring's random jostling, so it steps mostly one way. Nearly a full turn later, the proton leaves into the matrix. The ring is bolted to a bent shaft, gamma.
scenes.caption: The gradient biases the ring's random jostling, so it steps mostly one way. Nearly a full turn later, the proton leaves into the matrix. The ring is bolted to a bent shaft, gamma.
scenes.visual: The ring jitters back and forth in small random twitches, but each forward twitch catches a new YELLOW proton from the upper half channel, so net motion is one way (arrow labelled 'mostly one way'). Follow one marked proton: it rides the ring nearly all the way round (the drum turns about 315 degrees), then drops out through a second tunnel in the a subunit, open only to the matrix below. On 'bent shaft', a bright GREEN rod extends down out of the ring's centre into the head below the membrane, visibly bent near its lower end, labelled 'gamma shaft'; it turns with the ring. One full ring turn = 8 protons; each proton steps the ring 45 degrees (360 / 8).

scenes.tts: The shaft reaches into the head, in the matrix. Three alpha and three beta subunits sit around it like orange segments. The bent shaft presses differently on each beta, holding each in its own shape.
scenes.narration: The shaft reaches into the head, in the matrix. Three alpha and three beta subunits sit around it like orange segments. The bent shaft presses differently on each beta, holding each in its own shape.
scenes.caption: The shaft reaches into the head, in the matrix. Three alpha and three beta subunits sit around it like orange segments. The bent shaft presses differently on each beta, holding each in its own shape.
scenes.visual: Camera swings to look straight down the shaft axis at the head: the head becomes a top-down ring of six segments, alternating pale 'alpha' and GREEN-outlined 'beta' (label one of each only), around a central GREEN off-centre lobe (the bent shaft seen end-on). The membrane ring shrinks to a small side-view inset at upper left, still turning slowly with YELLOW protons dropping in. On 'presses differently', the lobe turns slowly; the beta segment it presses against squeezes narrower, the other two betas take different widths, so the three betas are visibly three different shapes.

scenes.tts: Each beta subunit is where A T P is made, from A D P and phosphate. So what does the proton's energy buy? Making the bond, or something else?
scenes.narration: Each beta subunit is where ATP is made, from ADP and phosphate. So what does the proton's energy buy? Making the bond, or something else?
scenes.caption: Each beta subunit is where ATP is made, from ADP and phosphate. So what does the proton's energy buy? Making the bond, or something else?
scenes.visual: In one beta segment a GOLD ADP dot and an ORANGE phosphate dot sit side by side; a short thin line flickers between them labelled 'new bond'. A YELLOW glow, the proton's energy, travels from the inset ring up the shaft and stops at the head, hovering. Question card at top in white: 'What does the energy buy?' Two small option tags under it: 'the bond?' and 'something else?'.

Predict pause. The question card and both option tags stay. The YELLOW glow hovers at the hub; the inset ring turns very slowly; the GOLD and ORANGE dots bob gently in their beta site. No other change.

scenes.tts: Paul Boyer turned the question inside out. As the shaft turns, each beta site cycles through three shapes. Open takes in A D P and phosphate. Loose holds them. In Tight, A T P forms on its own, held too firmly to leave.
scenes.narration: Paul Boyer turned the question inside out. As the shaft turns, each beta site cycles through three shapes. Open takes in ADP and phosphate. Loose holds them. In Tight, ATP forms on its own, held too firmly to leave.
scenes.caption: Paul Boyer turned the question inside out. As the shaft turns, each beta site cycles through three shapes. Open takes in ADP and phosphate. Loose holds them. In Tight, ATP forms on its own, held too firmly to leave.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves. Tag at top left: 'Boyer'. The three beta segments get large state labels in TEXT: 'open', 'loose', 'tight'. On 'Open takes in', the open segment widens and a GOLD ADP and ORANGE phosphate dot drift in from the matrix. On 'Loose holds them', the segment holding them narrows slightly, the dots sitting apart. On 'In Tight', the third segment clamps shut; its GOLD and ORANGE dots merge into one GREEN square with no flash and no YELLOW glow (it costs almost nothing), and the clamped segment holds the square fast, the square straining but unable to leave.

scenes.tts: On the enzyme, making the bond costs almost nothing. Here is the idea. Protons turn the shaft, and the turning pays above all to pry finished A T P loose. It also drives the binding of A D P and phosphate.
scenes.narration: On the enzyme, making the bond costs almost nothing. Here is the idea. Protons turn the shaft, and the turning pays above all to pry finished ATP loose. It also drives the binding of ADP and phosphate.
scenes.caption: On the enzyme, making the bond costs almost nothing. Here is the idea. Protons turn the shaft, and the turning pays above all to pry finished ATP loose. It also drives the binding of ADP and phosphate.
scenes.visual: On 'costs almost nothing', a small energy bar beside the tight site labelled 'bond' stays nearly empty. On 'Protons turn the shaft', YELLOW protons drop through the inset ring and the GREEN lobe turns 120 degrees; the YELLOW glow flows up the shaft into the tight site, which springs open, and the GREEN square flies out into the matrix. A second bar labelled 'release' fills tall. On 'binding of ADP and phosphate', a smaller share of the YELLOW glow goes to the open site as new GOLD and ORANGE dots are pulled in; a third bar labelled 'binding' fills partway. Bar heights are schematic (no numbers). Line at bottom: 'energy goes to letting go'.

scenes.tts: Each one hundred twenty degree turn moves every site one step and releases one A T P. John Walker later caught all three in one crystal. One site held an A T P look-alike, one A D P, and one was empty.
scenes.narration: Each one hundred twenty degree turn moves every site one step and releases one ATP. John Walker later caught all three in one crystal. One site held an ATP look-alike, one ADP, and one was empty.
scenes.caption: Each one hundred twenty degree turn moves every site one step and releases one ATP. John Walker later caught all three in one crystal. One site held an ATP look-alike, one ADP, and one was empty.
scenes.visual: The energy bars fade. The GREEN lobe turns in three clean 120-degree steps; at each step all three labels shift one segment forward (loose to tight, tight to open, open to loose) and one GREEN square leaves; a counter at right reads '1', '2', '3 ATP per turn' (shown, not narrated here). On 'John Walker', the motion freezes like a photograph: a white frame snaps around the head, tag 'Walker: one crystal'. Inside the frozen head the three betas show a GREEN-outlined square labelled 'ATP look-alike', a GOLD dot labelled 'ADP', and an empty site labelled 'empty'. The inset ring keeps turning so the frame is not frozen for more than 4 s.

scenes.tts: Now count the price. The vertebrate ring has eight c subunits, the smallest known. Eight protons make one full turn, which releases three A T P. That is about two point seven protons per A T P.
scenes.narration: Now count the price. The vertebrate ring has eight c subunits, the smallest known. Eight protons make one full turn, which releases three ATP. That is about two point seven protons per ATP.
scenes.caption: Now count the price. The vertebrate ring has eight c subunits, the smallest known. Eight protons make one full turn, which releases three ATP. That is about two point seven protons per ATP.
scenes.visual: The photo frame dissolves; the camera returns to the side view so ring, shaft and head all show, filling about 70% of the frame height. Tag: 'vertebrate ring'. The 8 ring segments light one at a time as 8 YELLOW protons drop in, the ring advancing 45 degrees per proton; at the end of one full turn three GREEN squares have left the head. A large tally at right builds: '8 protons', '3 ATP', then '8 / 3 = 2.7 per ATP'.

scenes.tts: A translocase then swaps each A T P out of the matrix for A D P. That swap moves charge, so the voltage takes a toll. Phosphate comes in with a proton too. Together, about three point seven protons per exported A T P.
scenes.narration: A translocase then swaps each ATP out of the matrix for ADP. That swap moves charge, so the voltage takes a toll. Phosphate comes in with a proton too. Together, about three point seven protons per exported ATP.
scenes.caption: A translocase then swaps each ATP out of the matrix for ADP. That swap moves charge, so the voltage takes a toll. Phosphate comes in with a proton too. Together, about three point seven protons per exported ATP.
scenes.visual: Two small fixed doors appear in the membrane band to the right of the synthase, labelled 'translocase' and 'phosphate carrier'. On 'swaps each ATP out', a GREEN square passes up through the translocase while a GOLD dot comes down; a tiny YELLOW chip labelled 'toll' is taken from the gradient above. On 'Phosphate comes in', an ORANGE dot and a YELLOW proton come down through the phosphate carrier together. The tally at right adds '+ about 1' under '2.7' and resolves to 'about 3.7 per exported ATP'.

scenes.tts: Follow one proton. It rides the ring nearly once around, and pays for an eighth of a turn. The bond costs almost nothing. What the proton buys, above all, is the moment a finished A T P lets go.
scenes.narration: Follow one proton. It rides the ring nearly once around, and pays for an eighth of a turn. The bond costs almost nothing. What the proton buys, above all, is the moment a finished ATP lets go.
scenes.caption: Follow one proton. It rides the ring nearly once around, and pays for an eighth of a turn. The bond costs almost nothing. What the proton buys, above all, is the moment a finished ATP lets go.
scenes.visual: Tally and carrier doors fade. One YELLOW proton glows brighter than the rest; it drops into the ring, rides nearly once around as the ring and GREEN shaft turn together, and leaves into the matrix; a tag beside it reads 'its share: 45 degrees' (one eighth, 360 / 8, since eight protons ride the ring at once). Camera follows the shaft up to the head: the tight site with its GREEN square sits calm (bond already made). On 'lets go', the tight site opens and the GREEN square floats free into the matrix, glowing YELLOW at its edge for a moment.

End card over the dimmed but still moving synthase world (YELLOW protons dropping through the slowly turning GREEN ring, GREEN squares leaving the head). Large white text, centred: 'Protons turn the rotor; the turning pays mainly to release ATP.'
